Solon Land-Clearing Knowledge

What to Check Before You Clear a Solon Lot

Before any Solon clearing job breaks ground, Roubic confirms property lines and calls in a utility locate through Ohio 811 (the Ohio Utilities Protection Service) — a free, legally required step statewide before mechanical clearing near buried gas, electric, water, or communication lines. It protects the property and keeps the crew safe.

Larger clearing jobs may involve local zoning, right-of-way, or stormwater/erosion considerations. Solon's specific permitting depends on the parcel and scope, so Roubic reviews requirements with you during the on-site walk rather than assuming — no surprises once the work starts.

What Happens If You Defer

The Cost of Waiting — Solon Context

Three ways a manageable clearing job grows into a bigger, costlier one when it's put off.

Undergrowth Spreads Fast

Brush, saplings, and invasive undergrowth thicken every growing season. What is a one-day clearing today becomes denser, slower, and more expensive to clear a year or two out.

Overgrown Trees Reach Structures

Unmanaged growth along fence lines and lot edges eventually crowds fences, sheds, and garages — turning simple clearing into removal-over-structure work at a higher cost.

Drainage & Erosion Problems

Overgrown, root-bound parcels can trap water and worsen erosion. Clearing and re-grading early is far cheaper than fixing drainage damage after it starts.

Common Solon Land-Clearing Questions

Solon Land Clearing FAQ

Six things Solon property owners want to know before booking a clearing job.

Do I need a permit to clear land in Solon?
It depends on the parcel and the scope of the work. Some clearing is routine private-property work, while larger jobs can involve local zoning, right-of-way, or stormwater/erosion rules. Because requirements vary by lot, Roubic reviews what applies to your specific property during the free on-site walk rather than assuming — and always calls in an Ohio 811 utility locate before any mechanical clearing.
How fast can Roubic clear land in Solon?
Solon is a Tier 1 Roubic service area — priority estimate scheduling during business hours (Mon–Fri 7am–6pm) and a 1–2 hour on-site response for after-hours storm and emergency calls via our 24/7 line. Most clearing jobs are scheduled shortly after the estimate is approved; timing depends on parcel size and vegetation density.
How much does land clearing cost in Solon?
Land clearing is quoted per job rather than off a fixed price list. Cost depends on parcel size, how dense the brush and trees are, the terrain, stump handling, and how much debris has to be hauled off. Aaron confirms a free, written price on-site after walking the property, so you know the number before any work begins.
Does Roubic handle full lot clearing for new construction?
Yes — Roubic clears wooded and overgrown lots for new builds, including trees, saplings, brush, and stump grinding to leave the site ready for grading. Because we own our chippers, tracked equipment, and grinders, the whole job stays with one family crew instead of being split among subcontractors.
Do you haul away the debris after clearing?
Yes — haul-off is part of the job. Brush and wood are chipped and removed, and larger material is hauled off-site so you're left with a clean, usable parcel. What's included is confirmed in your written estimate before the crew starts.
Are you insured for land-clearing work in Solon?
Yes — Roubic carries general liability insurance and workers-compensation coverage. A certificate of insurance is available on request and included in the estimate packet for jobs that require COI submission, which is common for property managers and commercial clearing work.
